How to set a realistic deadline for your goal.

Why we stop doing things we know are good for us, reason #23: the guessed deadline. Arjun gives himself 4 weeks for his portfolio. Week 4, it's half done, he feels behind and stops opening it. The goal was fine. The date was a guess from the best case.

In one study (Buehler, Griffin & Ross, 1994), students guessed their thesis would take about 34 days. It took about 56.

The fix: before you set a date, ask how long the last similar thing actually took you, and plan that.

Slow down until it's clean. Ten clean reps. Then speed up a little. Still clean? Speed up again. Typing, guitar, a tennis serve: same rule.

Why we stop doing things we know are good for us, reason #25: autopilot. Month one, you go from nothing to five songs. Then months of the same five songs, and your level doesn't move. The fix, every session:
- Notice what feels easy
- Add one thing just out of reach (the song 5 beats faster, one page that's a bit too hard)

items.ig_caption:
How to see your progress when you feel stuck: the Sunday test.

Why we stop doing things we know are good for us, reason #29: invisible progress. Tara practised singing 20 minutes a day for two months and every day sounded like the day before. You compare today with yesterday, and one day of practice is too small to notice. The change only shows across weeks.

The fix, the Sunday test:
- Same test every week (same song, same 2 km, same prompt)
- Never delete one
- In week 8, play week 1 first

What would you record every Sunday? Tell me below.

Dmyor: archive your dream today, break it into steps you can actually do. Link in bio.

#progress #selfimprovement #singing #motivation #consistency
